searchText: <cryptodavidw> Yoyo <cryptodavidw> /me trying to understand the altair spec. Wondering why there are finality updates with empty next sync committee and normal updates. Aren't all updates finalized? <etan_status> the signature_slot determines the signing sync committee if attested_slot is from an earlier sync committee, you already have to know the next sync committee in order to validate the message, so it doesnt make sense to include the same sync committee as part of the update <etan_status> if you are referring to the reason why there is LightClientFinalityUpdate and LightClientOptimisticUpdate, thats just to reduce message size. finality only changes at max every epoch, and the sync committee only changes every 8192 slots <cryptodavidw> refering to this BTW <cryptodavidw> (helios implementation) <cryptodavidw> > if attested_slot is from an earlier sync committee, you already have to know the next sync committee in order to validate the message I think I'm confused as to why there is both an attested and a finalized header, and why they can be in different sync period. Isn't the finalized_header the one that matters here and that should be verifiyable with your current sync committee? <etan_status> the attested_header is the one being signed the signature_slot is the slot at which the sig was made (usually attested +1 but can be more) the finalized header is the finalized_checkpoint.rootat attested_header.beacon.state_root its documented in the consensus-specs repo <cryptodavidw> oh OK I see that now <cryptodavidw> so finalized_header is not of type LightClientHeader here right? <cryptodavidw> perhaps from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=85MeiMA4dD8 I understand that the sync committee signs a block, which is a parent of the attested_header, which is a parent of the finalized_header <etan_status> re: **@cryptodavidw** > perhaps from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=85MeiMA4dD8 I understand that the sync committee signs a block, which is a parent of the attested_header, which is a parent of the finalized_header slot number increases from left to right. the sync committee signature is included in the red block to the right. it signs the parent block (blue / attested_header) that one's post state_root has a finalized_checkpoint.root that refers to the green block. green block < blue block < red block. everything up to the green block is finalized (meaning, there is only a single canonical chain / no more reorgs). everything up to the blue block is attested (meaning, the sync committee believes it will become canonical, but there may still be reorgs). the red block just contains the signature, but it was not signed itself yet (so we cannot assume it is valid yet) <etan_status> finalized is an ancestor of attested (about ~64-96 slots between normally) attested is the parent of the signature block <cryptodavidw> oh wow OK this makes it really clear, thanks so much for that answer! <cryptodavidw> so it is clearly a PBFT-style chain happening on top of the blocks <etan_status> well, it's a simplified view over that, so that a light client can follow it without running the full state transition validation <cryptodavidw> BTW it would be nice to have an overview in the spec, and some text on rationales. I don't know if the altair spec is set in stone at this point, but it's not always clear what are the intentions and how functions are supposed to be used by the implementor Etan's videos are perfect for understanding the concepts. And feel free to ask any questions here. <cryptodavidw> BTW the only difference between a finality update and an update is that the finality update omits the next_sync_comittee with it right? <etan_status> yes, you only need 1 full update per sync committee period. the process is described here: - https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/light-client/light-client.md <etan_status> generally, the ethereum/consensus-specs repo does not offer rationale. the light client spec are consistent in that regard with the rest. @jtraglia

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <cryptodavidw> /me trying to understand the altair spec. Wondering why there are finality updates with empty next sync committee and normal updates. Aren't all updates finalized?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<etan_status> the signature_slot determines the signing sync committee

if attested_slot is from an earlier sync committee, you already have to know the next sync committee in order to validate the message, so it doesnt make sense to include the same sync committee as part of the update

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <etan_status> if you are referring to the reason why there is LightClientFinalityUpdate and LightClientOptimisticUpdate, thats just to reduce message size. finality only changes at max every epoch, and the sync committee only changes every 8192 slots

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<cryptodavidw> > if attested_slot is from an earlier sync committee, you already have to know the next sync committee in order to validate the message

I think I'm confused as to why there is both an attested and a finalized header, and why they can be in different sync period. Isn't the finalized_header the one that matters here and that should be verifiyable with your current sync committee?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<etan_status> the attested_header is the one being signed

the signature_slot is the slot at which the sig was made (usually attested +1 but can be more)

the finalized header is the finalized_checkpoint.rootat attested_header.beacon.state_root

its documented in the consensus-specs repo

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <cryptodavidw> perhaps from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=85MeiMA4dD8 I understand that the sync committee signs a block, which is a parent of the attested_header, which is a parent of the finalized_header

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<etan_status> re: **@cryptodavidw**
> perhaps from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=85MeiMA4dD8 I understand that the sync committee signs a block, which is a parent of the attested_header, which is a parent of the finalized_header
slot number increases from left to right.

the sync committee signature is included in the red block to the right.

it signs the parent block (blue / attested_header)

that one's post state_root has a finalized_checkpoint.root that refers to the green block.

green block < blue block < red block.

everything up to the green block is finalized (meaning, there is only a single canonical chain / no more reorgs).

everything up to the blue block is attested (meaning, the sync committee believes it will become canonical, but there may still be reorgs).

the red block just contains the signature, but it was not signed itself yet (so we cannot assume it is valid yet)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<etan_status> finalized is an ancestor of attested (about ~64-96 slots between normally)

attested is the parent of the signature block
